Item 10.12
No. .2024 In The High Court At Calcutta
01 Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction

APPELLATE SIDE Ct 22  CRR 3659 of 2019 rup IA NO: CRAN 6 of 2023  CRAN 8 of 2024  (Assigned)
 Sri Sushil Kumar Mohanka & Ors.
 Vs.
 State of West Bengal & Anr.
 Mr. Krishnendu Bhattacharya,
 Mr. Avishem Guha,
 Mr. Ankush Majumdar.
 ... for the petitioners.
 Mr. Sayanta Bose,
 Ms. Priyanka Gope.

... for the opposite party No.2.
 Mr. Arijit Ganguly,
 Mr. Debjani Sahu. ... for the State.

In No. CRAN 8 of 2024  1.
Petitioner No.3, Aditya Vikram Mohanka and opposite party No.2, Ishita Mohanka are present before this Court in terms of direction of this Court, pursuant to an application for joint compromise filed in connection with the instant application.

According to joint compromise petition the de facto complainant/opposite party herein put the law in motion initially by lodging FIR alleging incidents happened to her at the instance of all three petitioners of the revisional application and that complaint was registered as Newtown Police Station Case No. 437 of 2018 dated 11.10.2018 under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Newtown Police Station Case No. 437 of 2018
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Investigation was ended with chargesheet.

2. The instant revisional application has been filed with a prayer for quashing that proceeding and in course of pendency of this revisional application, one joint compromise petition has been filed stating, inter alia, that difference between the parties has already been patched up and all other proceeding pending between the petitioner No.3 and opposite party No.2 were withdrawn.

Now by filing this joint compromise petition both the parties to this revisional application have prayed for Sri Sushil Kumar Mohanka & Ors vs State Of West Bengal & Anr on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122665435/
1 quashing of the proceeding in connection with G.R. Case No. 4312 of 2018 arising out of Newtown Police Station Case No. 437 of 2018.

entities.text: Newtown Police Station Case No. 437 of 2018
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State is also present by handing over Case Diary to this Court.
I have gone through the Case Diary.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State has raised no objection if the matter has been settled between the parties particularly, opposite party No.2 and petitioner No.3 (wife and husband).
4.

I have gone through the Case Diary and all other documents annexed with this revisional application and I find that both the opposite party No.2 and petitioner No.3 settled their existing dispute between the parties and opposite party No.2 who is present before this Court has also expressed her wiliness to withdraw the prosecution case which is pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat, North 24 Parganas in connection with G.R. Case No. 4312 of 2018.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat, North 24 Parganas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. Considering all facts and circumstances, I do not find any reason to stand in the way while both the opposite party No.2 and petitioner No.3 have already been settled the dispute between the parties, otherwise it would be a glaring example of abuse of process of Court.

6. Regard being had to the above, the proceeding in connection with G.R. Case No. 4312 of 2018 arising out of Newtown Police Station Case No. 437 of 2018 pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat, North 24 Parganas stands quashed.

entities.text: Newtown Police Station Case No. 437 of 2018
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barasat, North 24 Parganas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. With this observation, the revisional application along with CRAN 8 of 2024 stands disposed of.
8. Other connected applications, if any, stand disposed of.
9. Personal appearance of the opposite party No.2 and petitioner No.3 stands dispensed with.
10. Urgent photostat certified copy of the order, if applied for, be given to the parties on usual undertakings.
11. All parties shall act on the server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Bibhas Ranjan De, J.)
